name: What is an Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU)?

mainEntity.name: What is an Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU)?

acceptedAnswer.text: An Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU), also known as a granny flat, in-law unit, or secondary dwelling, is a smaller, independent residential living unit located on the same lot as a primary single-family home. It includes a kitchen, bathroom, and sleeping area, functioning as a complete home. ADUs can be detached, attached, or converted from existing space like a garage. They offer versatile solutions for additional living space, rental income, or housing family members.
acceptedAnswer.description: An ADU is a secondary, independent living unit on the same property as a primary home, complete with kitchen, bathroom, and sleeping area.
